final.markdown:
# Formal Complaint regarding Cyber Fraud and Unauthorized Credit Card Transaction

**To:** The Station House Officer, [POLICE STATION] Police Station (submit at the police station or on your state police portal)

This letter is a formal request to the Station House Officer at [POLICE STATION] to register an FIR regarding a cyber fraud incident. It details how you were misled by a caller claiming to be from Axis Bank, which led to an unauthorized debit from your credit card. The letter asks the police to investigate the matter, trace the stolen funds, and provide you with a copy of the FIR.

```
To,
The Station House Officer
[POLICE STATION] Police Station


Date: 09 October 2026

Subject: Formal Complaint regarding Cyber Fraud and Unauthorized Credit Card Transaction

Dear Sir/Madam,

I am writing to formally report a cyber fraud incident that occurred on [DATE AND TIME OF INCIDENT] at [PLACE OF INCIDENT]. I received a phone call from an individual claiming to be a representative of Axis Bank. During the call, I was directed to click on a specific URL. Immediately after accessing this link, an unauthorized transaction was processed, resulting in the debit of [AMOUNT] from my credit card. I request you to register an FIR regarding this incident and provide me with a free copy of the same. I urge you to initiate an investigation into this fraudulent activity, trace the destination of the funds, and take necessary steps to freeze the amount. I am prepared to provide all relevant transaction details and evidence to assist in your inquiry.

Yours faithfully,
[YOUR NAME]
[PHONE]
[EMAIL]
[ADDRESS]

Keep a copy and ask for a signed, stamped receipt (or the FIR copy) when you submit this.
```

## Where to report, and if the police don't act
1. **National Cyber Crime Helpline 1930 / cybercrime.gov.in** (call 1930 · report on cybercrime.gov.in · call your bank to block the account/card) — Immediately — within hours if possible, so the money can be traced and frozen. Note the acknowledgement number and quote it in your police complaint. https://cybercrime.gov.in · 1930
2. **Station House Officer (SHO), [POLICE STATION]** (written complaint at the police station · e-FIR on your state police citizen portal where available) — Give your written complaint at the police station. For a cognizable offence the police must register an FIR; you can report at any police station (zero FIR) and you are entitled to a free copy. Get a signed and stamped receipt for your written complaint. · 112
3. **Superintendent of Police / Deputy Commissioner of Police** (complaint in writing by registered post or in person) — If the SHO refuses to register an FIR: send the substance of your complaint in writing to the SP/DCP (BNSS, 2023, s.173(4)). Keep the postal receipt.
4. **Judicial Magistrate** (application through a lawyer or the District Legal Services Authority (free if eligible)) — If the police still do not act: apply to the Magistrate to direct registration and investigation (BNSS, 2023, s.175(3)). https://nalsa.gov.in · 15100

_Information, not legal advice._
